[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p551/r6] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · النبي، وأبي بن كعب | reports | A report says the Prophet omitted a verse in prayer; when he asked why Ubayy did not remind him, Ubayy said he feared it had been removed, and the Prophet replied that he had forgotten it. No grading is given.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p551/r7] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | With hamza, the word comes from delaying; Arab usage includes delaying camels' watering by a day or more.

[SAMIN-DURR:2:106#5/r2] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | rejects | Al-Samīn calls the alternative remote because مثلها does not naturally coordinate with بخير on that meaning; attachment to منها without repeating the preposition is Kufan-only.

[SAMIN-DURR:2:106/r8] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · الزمخشري | reports | Al-Zamakhsharī treats the hamza as causative, with Gabriel omitted as first object; الإنساخ is commanding or informing him of abrogation.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:106/r9] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · ابن عطية | reports | Ibn ʿAṭiyya also treats the hamza as causative but supplies the Prophet as omitted object and takes الإنساخ as permission to leave an abrogated āya.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p375#2/r1] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn Abbas explains naskh as replacing one verse with another.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p375#2/r10] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · ابن جرير | reports | For Ibn Jarir, abrogation applies to commands, prohibitions, restrictions, permissions and legal rulings, not to reports; changing either a verse’s ruling or its wording is called abrogation.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p375#2/r11] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · علماء الأصول | reports | Legal theorists phrase the definition differently, but the matter is close; a common summary is lifting a ruling through later legal evidence, including replacement by a lighter or heavier ruling or no replacement, while detailed types and conditions belong to legal theory.

[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p375#2/r13] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · author | holds | Ibn Kathir grades the report about the two men as weak because Sulayman ibn Arqam is weak.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p375#2/r14] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · الزهري | reports | Al-Zuhri reads nunsiha with a damma on the initial nun and without doubling it.
